headline: Meta's AI spending bill sparks a 6.7% chip rout; Nasdaq −2.6% while yields tumble below 5%
summary: A one-sided tech sell-off. Futures slid overnight after Meta, Tesla and Lam Research reported, and the selling deepened through the day: the Nasdaq had its worst day since June and the S&P 500 its worst since July, both closing near their lows. Under the surface the market held up — the Dow and Russell 2000 ended slightly higher, NYSE gainers edged out losers, and staples, defense and industrials rallied as money rotated out of AI names and into Treasuries.
drivers: Meta beat on revenue but posted negative free cash flow of $2.1B, its first cash burn in more than a decade, raised the low end of its capex range to $135B and plans a 2-for-1 split into non-voting shares to help fund AI spending; the stock fell 7%. Tesla lost 3.1% despite positive free cash flow and a cut in 2026 capex to about $20B.
Chips suffer their worst day since June

The SOX sank 6.7% to its lowest close since Jul 29, now more than 26% below its June record. Lam Research fell about 12% on an outlook only in line and supply-chain limits; AMD, Intel, Sandisk and Marvell dropped more than 8%, Micron about 6%, CoreWeave 11% and Nvidia 4% after Jensen Huang said a lack of capital is holding back neocloud growth.
Oil jumps on Iran strike plans

A report that the US and Israel have drawn up renewed strikes on Iran for after the Nov 3 midterms, plus more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, sent Brent up 4% to $113.17, its highest settle in over five months; WTI rose 2.4% to $99.47. Gold fell nearly 3%.
Bonds rally, defensives catch a bid

The 10-year yield fell about 18bp to 4.96%, below 5% for the first time since Sep 23, in the biggest Treasury rally in about a year; jobless claims dropped to 194K. Procter & Gamble rose 5.6% and Lockheed Martin 7% on beats, Blackstone 8.4% and Spotify 11.1%, while Moderna sank nearly 20%.
week: Week so far: Russell 2000 +2.3%, Dow +1.7%, S&P 500 +0.1%, Nasdaq −0.5%, as Thursday wiped out most of the week's chip rebound. Oil above $110 Brent keeps inflation in focus, and markets still see a chance of another 25bp Fed hike before year-end.
watch: Next: Western Digital beat and guided well above forecasts after the close but gave back an early 4% after-hours gain; Friday brings flash PMIs and consumer sentiment, then the Fed decides Oct 28 alongside Microsoft and SK hynix results, with Intel on Oct 29.
